A1.justification: Both PDFs describe HYPOTHESAES, with matching research objectives, experiments, and theoretical framework. All 25 pages of each version, including tables, figures, equations, proofs, and appendix prompts, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations on three synthetic tasks and three real-world tasks, comparative results in Tables 1–6, and supporting experiments in Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains these original evaluations, numerical results, and appendix experiments.

M1.justification: The reported SAE formulation changes: Equation (5) adds pre-encoder bias subtraction and ReLU, while Appendix B.1 changes the auxiliary objective from input reconstruction using additional top activations to residual reconstruction using dead neurons. These are limited formulation revisions within the retained three-step pipeline; the PDFs do not establish that the implementation changed.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate WIKI-5, WIKI-15, BILLS, HEADLINES, YELP, and CONGRESS with the same task requirements. The added explanation of pairwise headline processing does not introduce a new task or dataset.

E2.justification: BERTopic, NLPARAM, and HypoGeniC remain the comparators in Table 2. The n-gram and Batista and Ross comparisons in Section 6.3, and the comparison strategies in the appendix experiments, are also retained.

E3.justification: Appendix A revises the reported CONGRESS sampling rule: v1 describes retaining up to five chunks per speech before splitting; v2 specifies an exception restricting heldout data to one chunk per speech. Split totals and evaluation metrics remain unchanged. This establishes a revision to the written protocol, without establishing experimental reruns.

E4.justification: The SAE-NOVAL ablation, fidelity-selection experiment, interpretation-strategy comparisons, and pipeline performance-loss analysis are all retained in Appendices B.2 and C. The expanded sampling discussion and relocated figures do not add an analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same Bonferroni correction, paired t-tests, five sampled surface-similarity judgments, and information about random sampling and interpretation candidates. No repeated-run or uncertainty-reporting practice is added or revised.

E6.justification: Tables 1–6 have identical result entries, and Figures 2–3 contain identical plots. Numerical findings in Sections 6 and Appendices B–C are unchanged. The newly qualified CONGRESS protocol is not accompanied by replacement scores.

T1.justification: The encoder mapping in Equation (5) and the auxiliary-loss definition in Appendix B.1 receive non-equivalent mathematical revisions, including replacing full-input auxiliary reconstruction with residual reconstruction. The separation-score framework, Proposition 3.1, and its complete Appendix E proof remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: the theoretical connection between interpretation and hypothesis generation, the three-step SAE method, stronger hypothesis discovery, lower computational cost, and novel findings on HEADLINES and CONGRESS.

C2.justification: Appendix C.2 expands the rationale for high-weak sampling. v1 emphasizes balanced precision and recall; v2 explicitly connects overly specific top-random interpretations to reduced predictiveness and advises choosing sampling strategy according to desired hypothesis granularity.

D1.justification: v2 substantially expands reproduction information through a new Software and Data section providing installation instructions and links for code, a reproduction notebook, datasets, and a demo. Appendices A–C additionally disclose HEADLINES activation differencing, bias and weight initialization, decoder normalization, the 256-step dead-neuron threshold, and the distinction between released-code sampling defaults and experimental sampling.

R1.justification: The bibliography and central research positioning are unchanged. However, Appendix B.1 newly attributes feature splitting and specific SAE training practices to Bricken et al. (2023), and Figure 5 explicitly credits Zhong et al. (2024) for the surface-similarity prompt.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized revisions to the SAE description, preprocessing explanations, and sampling discussion; corrects the embedding-model name in the main text; updates acknowledgements; and adds Software and Data and Prompts headings. The main narrative and section sequence remain largely intact.

P2.justification: Figure 2 moves from page 17 to page 18, Figure 3 is repositioned within page 19, and appendix text and references reflow. Figure 5 gains an attribution sentence in its caption. No figure or table is added or removed, and their visual content is otherwise retained.

improvement.justification: v2 improves technical clarity and reproducibility through more explicit SAE and pairwise-input specifications, clearer holdout documentation, and concrete code/data access instructions. Disclosing that code defaults differ from experimental sampling also helps reproduction. These are useful gains, but the empirical results, supporting analyses, and central theoretical guarantee are unchanged, so the overall improvement is limited.
